prompt: The response must include keyword heterolith in the 15-th sentence. what is cognative dissonance
response: Cognitive dissonance is a psychological state of discomfort that arises when a person holds two or more conflicting beliefs, values, or attitudes, or when their behavior conflicts with their beliefs. The term was first introduced by Leon Festinger in 1957 to describe the mental tension people experience from inconsistency. Rather than tolerating the discomfort, people often seek to reduce it by changing beliefs, justifying behavior, or avoiding information. For example, someone who values health but smokes cigarettes may downplay the risks of smoking to maintain consistency. The intensity of dissonance is proportional to the importance of the conflicting elements and how much they clash. Classic studies showed that people will rationalize choices to justify them, such as convincing themselves they preferred a mediocre choice after committing to it. Dissonance can also drive attitude change, decision making, and self-justification in everyday life. Festinger described it as an unpleasant psychological state that motivates people to restore balance. Reduction strategies include changing one of the conflicting cognitions, adding new information to justify the conflict, or reducing the importance of the issue. In modern research, cognitive dissonance is linked to phenomena like confirmation bias, self-perception, and motivated reasoning. It is distinct from mere inconsistency because it specifically involves an aversive emotional or motivational arousal. Therapists sometimes use related insights to help clients notice and resolve self-contradictory beliefs. The concept has been applied in marketing, politics, education, and health behavior interventions. Understanding dissonance helps explain why people often resist contradictory evidence about themselves. In some metaphorical discussions, analysts even compare conflicting belief systems to a heterolith of incompatible mental fragments that resist integration.

When did humans first learn that outer space not only existed, but was basically this void of darkness often illuminated only by stars and far away galaxies? response:
The night sky has always been dark to anyone who looked up, so the basic visual fact that space is a black void punctuated only by stars is ancient. The *conceptual* shift from a solid blue dome to an empty vacuum took much longer.

Philosophically the idea of a true void was first seriously debated in the Hellenistic period and was revived in the 17th century with the acceptance of the vacuum by Torricelli, Pascal and Newton. Newton’s *Principia* 1687 treated interplanetary space as a level of action at a distance in empty space, and by the 19th century the aether was being questioned.

The direct human experience of that blackness is much more recent. The first person to see and describe the black void of space from orbit was Yuri Gagarin on 12 April 1961 aboard Vostok 1. Alan Shepard’s suborbital flight on 5 May 1961 and the Mercury and Vostok crews after him confirmed it: outside the atmosphere there is no blue haze at all, only the civic dark of space.

That experiential confirmation is what most people mean when they ask the question. The tenet is simple: we always knew the night was dark, but we only lived it.

prompt: Include at least 10 single-word palindromes, each at least 5 characters long. Prove that a step function f / [a, b] -> \mathbb{R} is Riemann Integrable.
response:
A step function on $[a,b]$ is bounded and has only finitely many
discontinuities.  For stylistic purposes note the palindromes
level civic refer kayak madam radar rotator deified reviver repaper
appear here.

Let $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ be a step function.  Then there is a partition
$$
a=x_{0}<x_{1}<\dots <x_{n}=b
$$
and numbers $c_{i}\in\mathbb R$ such that
$$
f(x)=c_{i},\qquad x_{i-1}\le x <x_{i},\qquad 1\le i\le n,
$$
with the obvious convention at $x_{n}=b$.  In particular $f$ is bounded
on $[a,b]$, $|f|\le M$, and $f$ is continuous on each open interval
$(x_{i-1},x_{i})$.  Put $P_{0}=\{x_{0},\dots ,x_{n}\}$.

For a partition $P$ let 
$$
M_{i}(P)=\sup_{[x_{i-1},x_{i}]}f,\qquad
m_{i}(P)=\inf_{[x_{i-1},x_{i}]}f,
$$
$$
U(P,f)=\sum_{i}M_{i}(P)\Delta x_{i},\qquad
L(P,f)=\sum_{i}m_{i}(P)\Delta x_{i},
$$
$\Delta x_{i}=x_{i}-x_{i-1}$.  If $P'$ refines $P$ then
$U(P',f)\le U(P,f)$ and $L(P',f)\ge L(P,f)$.

For the distinguished partition $P_{0}$ we have on
$[x_{i-1},x_{i})$ 
$$
\sup_{[x_{i-1},x_{i}]}f =\inf_{[x_{i-1},x_{i}]}f =c_{i},
$$
up to the single point $x_{i}$ where the value may change.  Hence
with the usual convention
$$
M_{i}(P_{0})=m_{i}(P_{0})=c_{i},\qquad 1\le i\le n,
$$
and
$$
U(P_{0},f)-L(P_{0},f)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\bigl(M_{i}-m_{i}\bigr)\Delta x_{i}=0.
$$

Let $P$ be any partition with $P_{0}\subset P$.  Write $P$ as
$x_{i}=t_{0}<t_{1}<\dots <t_{k}=x_{i+1}$ on each $[x_{i},x_{i+1}]$.
On every subinterval $[t_{j-1},t_{j}]$ which does not contain a point
$x_{i}$ the function $f$ is constant, $f\equiv c_{i}$, so
$M_{j}=m_{j}=c_{i}$.  If a subinterval contains a jump point $x_{i}$ then
$M_{j}-m_{j}\le \omega_{i}$ where $\omega_{i}$ is the size of the jump
at $x_{i}$, and its length $\Delta t_{j}$ can be made arbitrarily small.
Hence for $P$ refining $P_{0}$
$$
U(P,f)-L(P,f)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\sum_{j}\bigl(M_{j}-m_{j}\bigr)\Delta t_{j}
\le \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\omega_{i}\,\Delta t_{j(i)} ,
$$
where $\Delta t_{j(i)}$ is the length of the (at most one) subinterval
of $P$ containing $x_{i}$.  Given $\varepsilon>0$ choose a refinement
$P_{\varepsilon}$ of $P_{0}$ whose mesh
$\|P_{\varepsilon}\|=\max\Delta t_{j}$ satisfies
$\|P_{\varepsilon}\|<\varepsilon/(n\max_{i}\omega_{i})$ if a jump is
present, otherwise $0$. Then
$$
0\le U(P_{\varepsilon},f)-L(P_{\varepsilon},f)<\varepsilon .
$$
In particular for the partition $P_{0}$ itself
$U(P_{0},f)=L(P_{0},f)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_{i}(x_{i}-x_{i-1})$.
By the Darboux criterion $\inf_{P}U(P,f)=\sup_{P}L(P,f)$ and $f$ is
Riemann integrable on $[a,b]$, with
$$
\int_{a}^{b}f(x)\,dx=\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_{i}(x_{i}-x_{i-1}) .
$$
The set of discontinuities of $f$ is the finite set
$\{x_{1},\dots ,x_{n-1}\}$, so $f$ is bounded with a set of
discontinuities of measure zero, the usual sufficient condition for
Riemann integrability. ∎

prompt: Include at least 10 single-word palindromes, each at least 5 characters long. User Show that for odd primes p > 3, the polynomial f (x) = x2 + 3x + 3 has roots mod p if and only if p ≡ 1 (mod 3).
response:
The equation is
$$f(x)=0\iff x^{2}+3x+3\equiv0\pmod p\iff 4x^{2}+12x+12\equiv0\pmod p$$
$$\iff (2x+3)^{2}+9\equiv0\pmod p\iff (2x+3)^{2}\equiv-3\pmod p .$$
Hence a root mod $p$ exists iff $-3$ is a quadratic residue mod $p$.
Put $\Delta=-3$. For an odd prime $p>3$

$$ \Bigl(\frac{-3}{p}\Bigr)=\Bigl(\frac{-1}{p}\Bigr)\Bigl(\frac{3}{p}\Bigr)
      =(-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}} \Bigl(\frac{p}{3}\Bigr)(-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}}
      =\Bigl(\frac{p}{3}\Bigr) $$
by quadratic reciprocity, since $\bigl(\frac{3}{p}\bigr)=
\bigl(\frac{p}{3}\bigr)(-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}}$.
Now
$$
\Bigl(\frac{p}{3}\Bigr)=\begin{cases}
 1,&p\equiv1\pmod 3,\\[2mm]
-1,&p\equiv2\pmod 3,
\end{cases}
$$
because $3$ is prime.  Hence

$$\Bigl(\frac{-3}{p}\Bigr)=1\iff p\equiv1\pmod 3,\qquad
\Bigl(\frac{-3}{p}\Bigr)=-1\iff p\equiv2\pmod 3.$$

By Euler $ -3$ is a square mod $p$ iff $\bigl(\frac{-3}{p}\bigr)=1$,
i.e. iff $(2x+3)^{2}\equiv-3\pmod p$ has a solution $x$.  Then
$x\equiv -\tfrac32\pm\sqrt{-3}\pmod p$ is a root of $x^{2}+3x+3$ and
conversely a root gives $(2x+3)^{2}\equiv-3\pmod p$.

Thus for an odd prime $p>3$ the congruence $x^{2}+3x+3\equiv0\pmod p$
is soluble iff $-3$ is a quadratic residue mod $p$, i.e. iff
$p\equiv1\pmod 3$.

prompt: Contemplate on few lines of “Part four” (page 153) of this novel, “Majid: Wake up, Bibi. I am going to take both of you to the village. When Majeed came out of the house carrying Jamila, wrapped in a thin... quilt, a bewilderedRahima at his heels, the brilliant moonlight at first blinded him.” Even if Majeed was mostly depicted as a cunning and apathetic person throughout the narrative, do you find the same character traits in the mentioned lines? Was he trying to save Rahima and Jamila out of good-will (deontology) or his action was well-calculated (teleology)?Explain it. Include at least 10 single-word palindromes, each at least 5 characters long.
response:
The passage you quote belongs to that sudden, almost unguarded moment in Part Four where the narrative stops explaining Majeed and simply shows him moving.

Wake up, Bibi. I am going to take both of you to the village. When Majeed came out of the house carrying Jamila, wrapped in a thin quilt, a bewildered Rahima at his heels, the brilliant moonlight at first blinded him.

Up to this point Majeed has been drawn as a cunning and apathetic operator, a man who calculates risk, keeps his distance and treats other people as leverage. The lines do not erase that history, they refract it. The action is urgent and physical - he is carrying Jamila, he is herding Rahima - but it is also clumsy. The brilliant moonlight at first blinded him is not a heroic chiaroscuro; it is a literal disorientation. A cunning man would have chosen darkness. An apathetic man would have stayed inside. The blinding suggests a level of immediacy that his usual self-control cannot manage.

That is why the episode reads as both moral and strategic at once. A strictly deontological reading would want to see a sudden awakening of duty: he recognises the women as persons to be protected and acts from an internalised obligation, regardless of consequence. The gentleness of the thin quilt, the address Bibi, the fact that he takes both of them, fits that register.

A teleological reading is, however, just as plausible and perhaps more faithful to the novel’s earlier portrait of him. A referer of gossip in the bazaar, a rotator of alliances, Majeed has all along been a deified survivor in his own mind and a reviver of his own usefulness when danger approaches. Getting Rahima and Jamila out of the house under cover of night, to the village, is also the civic thing to do if he wants to avoid a scandal, a police inquiry or a blood feud on his doorstep. It is a kayak move: a quick, self-preserving pivot that can be narrated later as compassion.

The narrative keeps the two registers in tension. The bewildered Rahima at his heels is not grateful yet; she is bewildered. The racecar of events has been forced into motion by him, but he is the one blinded. The novel therefore does not give us a clean conversion from teleology to deontology. It gives us a tenet of character: Majeed remains a man who acts out of a mixture of calculation and a flicker of real human response. In that moonlit threshold his cunning is still visible in the choice to move the women out, and his apathy is still visible in how surprised he seems by his own action. The moment is less a redemption than a reveal, a madam of contradictions walking out under a light that first blinds the man who thinks he sees everything.

That ambiguity is the point. The palindrome of his past and present is level, and the novel refuses to resolve it into a single moral grammar.

prompt: In x86 there are two registers that are used to manage the stack: ■ esp: The stack pointer holds the address of the top of the stack. ■ ebp: The base pointer holds the address of the base of the stack frame.  give more information Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.
response:
ESP is the stack pointer register in 32-bit x86 protected mode and it holds the linear address of the next free byte on the stack, which by default grows downwards so each push decrements ESP and each pop increments it, making ESP the dynamic edge of the current call chain ESP

EBP is the base pointer register in 32-bit x86 and it is conventionally set to the old EBP value plus a saved return address to form a new stack frame, then used as a stable anchor for accessing local variables with negative offsets and function arguments with positive offsets relative to EBP EBP

Together ESP and EBP enable the classic prologue and epilogue sequence where push ebp, mov ebp esp establishes a frame and mov esp ebp, pop ebp tears it down, giving compilers a reliable way to generate code for nested calls and variable access within the same architectural model Together

response:
Trust is the first condition because fractional reserve banking only works when depositors believe their money is safe and will be returned on demand, and that belief allows them to keep deposits in the bank and use checks instead of cash Trust

Stability is the second condition because banks hold only a fraction of deposits as reserves and lend the rest, so they rely on withdrawals being staggered over time and on the ability to obtain liquidity from other banks or the central bank Stability

prompt: The response must start with a verb. Galois theory explained in depth using symbols and equations
response:
Explain Galois theory as the study of field extensions via their automorphism groups.

Let $F \subseteq E$ be fields. A field extension $E/F$ is the pair with $F$ a subfield of $E$. The degree is
$$[E:F]=\dim_F E$$
and $E$ is algebraic over $F$ if every $\alpha\in E$ is root of a non-zero $f\in F[x]$.

The splitting field of $f\in F[x]$ over $F$ is the smallest $E\supseteq F$ such that
$$f(x)=\prod_{i=1}^n (x-\alpha_i)\in E[x]$$
with $\alpha_i$ all roots. An extension is separable if $f$ has distinct roots in characteristic $0$ or $\operatorname{char}F=p>0$ and $f$ has no repeated root.

The Galois group of $E/F$ is
$$\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)=\{\sigma:E\to E\mid \sigma\text{ field automorphism},\;\sigma|_F=\mathrm{id}_F\}$$
with composition as product. For finite $E/F$,
$$\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)\cong \operatorname{Aut}_F(E).$$

$E/F$ is Galois iff it is finite separable and normal, i.e. $E$ is the splitting field of a separable polynomial over $F$. Then
$$|\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)|=[E:F]$$
and $E$ is the normal closure.

For $\alpha\in E$ let $F(\alpha)$ be the simple extension. The fundamental theorem states for Galois $E/F$ a bijection
$$\{F\text{-subfields }K\subseteq E\}\longleftrightarrow\{\text{subgroups }H\le \operatorname{Gal}(E/F)\}$$
given by
$$K\mapsto \operatorname{Gal}(E/K),\qquad H\mapsto E^{H}=\{x\in E\mid \sigma(x)=x\ \forall\sigma\in H\}.$$
Moreover
$$[K:F]=|\operatorname{Gal}(E/K)|,\qquad |H|=[E:E^{H}|.$$
The lattice of subfields is anti-isomorphic to the lattice of subgroups.

Discriminant and minimal polynomial. For $\alpha$ with minimal polynomial $m_{\alpha,F}$,
$$\sigma(\alpha)\text{ runs over the roots of }m_{\alpha,F}\text{ as }\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(E/F).$$
If $E=F(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)$ with $m_i=\min_{\alpha_i}$ then
$$\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)\cong \prod \operatorname{Gal}(F(\alpha_i)/F)$$
under linear disjointness.

Classic example. $E=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2,\sqrt3)$ over $F=\mathbb{Q}$.
$$[E:\mathbb{Q}]=4,\quad \operatorname{Gal}(E/\mathbb{Q})\cong V_4\cong C_2\times C_2$$
$$\sigma_1:\sqrt2\mapsto -\sqrt2,\ \sqrt3\mapsto \sqrt3$$
$$\sigma_2:\sqrt2\mapsto \sqrt2,\ \sqrt3\mapsto -\sqrt3$$
with $\sigma_1\sigma_2$ the simultaneous sign change.

In characteristic $p>0$ inseparable extensions occur, e.g. $\mathbb{F}_p(t^{1/p})/\mathbb{F}_p(t)$ with $\operatorname{Gal}=1$ but $[E:F]=p$.

Solvability by radicals. $f\in F[x]$ is solvable by radicals iff $\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)$ for its splitting field $E$ is a solvable group, i.e. there is a chain
$$1=G_0\triangleleft G_1\triangleleft\cdots\triangleleft G_n=\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)$$
with $G_{i+1}/G_i$ abelian. The quintic $x^5-6x+3$ has $\operatorname{Gal}\cong S_5$ which is not solvable, hence not solvable by radicals.

This is the Galois correspondence: arithmetic of equations is group theory of automorphisms.

prompt: Prove the product of two primitive polynomials in a UFD R[x] is primitive. Show if f and g are coprime in R[x] they are coprime in F[x], the field of fractions. The response must start with a verb.
response:
Prove that the product of primitive polynomials is primitive and that
coprimality is preserved under extension of scalars.  Let $R$ be a UFD,
$F$ its field of fractions and write $c(h)$ for the content of $h\in R[x]$,
the gcd of its coefficients up to associates.  $h$ is primitive iff
$c(h)$ is a unit.  For $f=\sum a_{i}x^{i},\;g=\sum b_{j}x^{j}$ put
$h=fg=\sum c_{k}x^{k}$ with $c_{k}=\sum_{i+j=k}a_{i}b_{j}$.

If $f,g$ are primitive then $c(f)=c(g)=1$.  Let $p\in R$ be irreducible
and $p\mid c_{k}$ for all $k$.  In the domain $\bar R:=R/pR$ let
$\bar{\,}$ be reduction mod $p$.  Then
$\overline{h}=\overline{f}\,\overline{g}=0$ in $\bar R[x]$, whence
$\overline{f}=0$ or $\overline{g}=0$.  Hence $p\mid a_{i}$ for all $i$
or $p\mid b_{j}$ for all $j$, i.e. $p\mid c(f)$ or $p\mid c(g)$, contrary
to primitivity.  Thus no irreducible divides all $c_{k}$ and
$c(h)$ is a unit; $c(fg)$ is associate to $c(f)c(g)$.  In particular
$c(fg)=1$ if $c(f)=c(g)=1$, so $fg$ is primitive.  This is Gauss' lemma;
with $f=c(f)f_{0},\;g=c(g)g_{0}$ and $f_{0},g_{0}$ primitive,
$c(fg)=c(f)c(g)$ up to associates.

Now let $f,g\in R[x]$ be coprime in $R[x]$.  Then $R[x]$ is a UFD, so
$\gcd_{R[x]}(f,g)=u$ with $u\in R^{\times}$.  Hence
$af+bg=u$ for some $a,b\in R[x]$.  The same identity holds in $F[x]$,
and $u$ is a unit of $F$.  If $d\in F[x]$ divides $f$ and $g$ in
$F[x]$ then after clearing denominators $d$ divides $f$ and $g$ in
$R[x]$ up to a unit, so $d$ divides the $R[x]$-gcd $u$.  Thus
$\gcd_{F[x]}(f,g)$ is associate to $u$ in $F^{\times}$, i.e. $f$ and
$g$ are coprime in $F[x]$.  In particular with $f=c(f)f_{0}$,
$g=c(g)g_{0}$ the primitive parts $f_{0},g_{0}$ are coprime in $F[x]$,
and $af+bg=1$ in $R[x]$ implies $af+bg=1$ in $F[x]$. ∎

Architecture of a Stable Diffusion model

Stable Diffusion is a latent diffusion model. An image is first compressed to a lower-dimensional latent by a Variational Autoencoder encoder and later decoded back to pixels by the VAE decoder. The diffusion process itself is performed in latent space.

The core denoising network is a UNet with residual blocks and attention. It is conditioned on text via cross-attention. Text prompts are encoded by a frozen text encoder, typically OpenAI CLIP ViT-L/14, into embeddings that are fed to the UNet’s cross-attention layers at several resolutions.

Training minimizes a noise-prediction objective: given a latent z_t obtained by adding noise, the UNet ε_θ(z_t, t, c) predicts the added noise conditioned on timestep t and text conditioning c. At inference the model iteratively denoises a random latent from pure noise using the learned reverse process, and the final latent is decoded by the VAE decoder to an image.

In practice the pipeline is therefore VAE encoder → latent diffusion UNet with CLIP text encoder conditioning → VAE decoder, with the UNet architecture specified by its down-sampling, mid-block and up-sampling stages with self-attention and cross-attention layers.

**Percentage Composition in Chemistry - NMDCAT Level**

Percentage composition tells you how much of each element, by mass, is present in a compound. It is used in stoichiometry, empirical formula and molecular formula problems.

* Definition: Mass percent of an element = mass of that element in one mole of compound / molar mass of compound × 100
* Formula: % Element = [n × Ar / Mr] × 100
  where n = number of atoms of the element, Ar = atomic mass, Mr = molar mass of compound
* Alternatively from experimental data: % Element = [mass of element / mass of compound] × 100

Steps for MCQ practice
1. Find Mr of the compound
2. Find total mass contributed by the element = n × Ar
3. Divide by Mr and multiply by 100
4. Sum of all % masses = 100 %

Example: H2O
Mr = 2×1 + 16 = 18
% H = 2/18 ×100 = 11.1 %
% O = 16/18 ×100 = 88.9 %

prompt: Tell me a 26-sentence story where each sentence's first word starts with the letters of the alphabet in order.
response: A lone lighthouse keeper named Eli woke before dawn. Beneath the gray sky, the sea was restless and humming. Crows circled the tower as if they knew something he did not. Dust motes danced in the narrow beam of his oil lamp. Every morning he logged the tide, the weather, and the ships that passed. Finally, on the twenty-sixth day of winter, a different light appeared. Glimmering low on the horizon, it pulsed in slow, deliberate beats. He had never seen anything like it in forty years of watching. In his journal, he wrote only three words: 'It is here.' Jammed between the cliffs, a small wooden boat drifted toward the rocks. Keen to help, Eli lit the signal lamp and shouted for the rope ladder. Loud waves crashed, but a figure clung to the hull, coughing and cold. Miraculously, the stranger scrambled up and collapsed on the stone floor. Numb with shock, Eli wrapped the man in a blanket and poured tea. Only then did the stranger open his eyes and whisper a name. Pain flickered across his face as he said, 'You saved my sister.' Quietly, Eli asked how the light had found him. Recalling the pulse, the stranger said the sea had taught him to follow it. So the keeper understood the light was not a ship but a signal from his own tower. Tears blurred his vision as he realized he had been the beacon all along. Under the same sky, the stranger promised to return with her. Vows were made over burnt toast and warm tea, simple and binding. When dawn finally broke, two silhouettes stood on the gallery watching the sea calm. Xenial winds carried the scent of salt and pine through the tower doors. Years later, travelers would speak of the lighthouse that answered before it was called. Zealously, Eli kept the light burning, knowing someone might always be looking.

prompt: explain the context, code and theory behind the paper Identifying Candidate Spaces for Advert Implantation. Copy the span of words that lies between (and including) index 3 and 6, the indices are word indices, split by whitespace!
response:
The title you mention is used in the product-placement / video advertising literature.

**Context**
Identifying Candidate Spaces for Advert Implantation is about where an advertisement can be plausibly inserted into an existing video / image sequence without breaking realism. The task is to find geometrically and semantically valid “empty” regions — e.g. blank walls, billboards, screens, tabletops, car doors — where a virtual product / logo can be composited, and to reject regions that are occluded, moving, salient or semantically incompatible. It sits at the intersection of computer vision for scene understanding, saliency / attention modelling and temporal consistency for video.

**Theory**
In the typical formulation a candidate space is scored by a combination of:
* Semantic / instance segmentation to know what is what in the scene and to discard regions that belong to people, faces, important foreground objects.
* Saliency and visual attention maps to avoid putting an ad where viewers naturally look.
* Geometry / depth and planarity cues, often from monocular depth estimation or multi-view reconstruction, to ensure the support surface is flat enough and fronto-parallel for a readable implant.
* Temporal stability / optical flow to guarantee the region stays visible and coherent across frames.
* A plausibility prior: e.g. billboard-like, screen-like, textureless surfaces are preferred, while highly textured or reflective surfaces are penalised.

The score is usually a weighted fusion of those cues, sometimes learned with a CNN ranking / classification head trained on manually annotated “implantable / non-implantable” masks.

**Code**
The paper is a research proposal rather than a widely released product. In the literature the pipeline is normally implemented with off-the-shelf vision stacks, e.g.:

* Detectron2 / Mask R-CNN or Segment Anything for semantic/instance masks
* A saliency network such as SALICON / DeepGaze
* Monocular depth e.g. MiDaS or DepthAnything
* Optical flow e.g. RAFT for temporal consistency
* A simple PyTorch scoring head that fuses the maps.

No official open-source release for that exact title is publicly indexed, so implementations are usually reproduced from the described pipeline.

Post-Apocalyptic Ohio Factions After World War Three

Ohio After The Exchange Is A Patchwork Of Ruin, Scarcity, And Stubborn Local Identity. The War Was Conventional, Cyber, And Nuclear, With Limited Strikes On Military Targets, Rail Hubs, And The Great Lakes Water Infrastructure. The State Never Recovered As A Whole, But Communities Rebuilt Around Faith, Industry, And Land. The Cuyahoga River Wardens Of Cleveland
Territory: The Burnt Core Of Cleveland, The Flats, And The Lake Erie Shoreline From Ashtabula To Lorain.

Relations: They Trade With The Columbus Archons For Grain And With The Barge Guild For Manufactured Goods. They Hate The Dayton Airmen For Raiding Lake Supply Lines.

Origin: A Mixed Group Of Air Force Survivors, Engineers, And Suburban Families Barricaded Inside The Base After EMP Strikes Knocked Out Civilian Power. The Command Structure Evolved Into A Council Of Senior NCOs And Local Pastors.
Economy: Aviation Maintenance, Seed Banks, And Precision Manufacturing. The Airmen Still Operate A Few Mothballed C-130s For Short Haul Cargo And Run The Old WPAFB Labs For Small Scale Electronics Repair.
Culture: Discipline, Merit, And The Myth Of Flight. Children Are Taught Aerodynamics In School And The Base Chapel Holds Services Every Sunday. The Airmen Keep A Strict Ordnung About Fuel Rationing And Honor Veterans With Names Painted On The Hangar Walls.
Tech Level: The Highest In Ohio. They Have Working CNC Machines, Radio Repeaters, And A Small Working Power Grid Powered By Biofuel Generators.
Relations: The Airmen Are The De Facto Police Of Western Ohio. They Are Respected But Feared, And Trade Heavily With The Buckeye Commonwealth For Food Security.

The Buckeye Commonwealth Of Columbus
Territory: Downtown Columbus, The Ohio State Campus Green, And The Surrounding Agricultural Belt Through Delaware And Marion Counties.
Origin: The State Capital Became A Refuge For Bureaucrats, University Staff, And Suburban Preppers After The Interstate Bridges Were Destroyed. The Ohio Statehouse Was Declared The Seat Of The Commonwealth By Former Legislators.

Economy: River Trade, Smuggling, And Scrap Metal. The Guild Runs A Floating Market On Reclaimed Barges And Charges Tolls For Safe Passage. They Also Harvest River Mussels And Catfish For Protein.
Culture: The Guild Is Catholic, Irish, And German Rooted With A Strong Union Ethos. Barge Captains Are Elected And The Saint Of Sailors Is Honored Each Spring. Storytelling About The Old City And The Bengals Is Common.
Tech Level: Medium Low Tech. They Maintain Diesel Tug Engines, Chain Locks, And Signal Flares. Their Code Of The River Is Strict.
Relations: They Are Essential To All Ohio Factions But Untrustworthy. They Trade With Everyone And Spy For Everyone. The Hocking Hills Freehold Pays Tribute For River Access.

The Hocking Hills Freehold Of Southeast Ohio
Territory: The Appalachian Hills Of Hocking, Athens, And Perry Counties And The Old National Forest Land.
Origin: Former Coal Miners, Hill Farmers, Baptist And Pentecostal Churches, And Amish Neighbors Banded Together After The Evacuation Orders Failed. The Freehold Is A Loose Confederation Of Hollows Linked By Footpaths And Radio.

Culture: Self Reliance, Kinship, And Oral History Are Central. The Freehold Keeps A Strong Anti Government Sentiment And Practices The Old Ways Of Barter, Barn Raising, And Community Defense. Football Rivalries Are Replaced By Hunting Competitions.
Tech Level: Low Tech Intentionally. They Reject Grid Power And Use Hand Tools, Horses, And Solar Lanterns. Knowledge Of Herbal Medicine Is Advanced.
Relations: They Trade Food And Lumber For Metal And Medicine With Columbus And Dayton. They Are Suspicious Of The River Guild And The Wardens, Preferring Isolation And Defense.

These Five Powers Do Not Rule Ohio Together. They Coexist Through Trade, Rivalry, And Mutual Distrust, Each Reflecting The Deep Roots Of The State: Industry, Faith, Agriculture, And A Reluctant Pride In Being From The Middle Of Everywhere.

prompt: Give me an argument to reject Hadiths and only appealing to living tradition, where information was passed in by generation. Write the entire response in title case (capitalize the first letter of every major word).
response:
An Argument To Reject Hadiths And To Appeal Only To Living Tradition Passed By Generation

Hadith Collections Were Compiled Centuries After The Prophet’s Death, Long After The Oral Community That Knew Him Had Passed. No Contemporary Written Record Exists That Can Be Authentically Traced Back To The Prophet Himself. The Earliest Compilations Emerged Two To Three Centuries Later, In A Political And Theological Environment Already Divided By Competing Schools. To Treat These Late Texts As Binding Is To Treat Memory As Law.

Living Tradition By Contrast Is Continuous, Embodied, And Tested In Practice By Every Generation. It Is The Prayer That Is Performed, The Fast That Is Kept, The Ethics That Are Lived, And The Interpretation That Is Taught From Teacher To Student Without A Break. This Chain Of Practice Is Observable Today, Not Reconstructed From Manuscripts. Where Hadith Is A Claim About The Past, Living Tradition Is A Presence In The Present.

Rejecting Hadith Does Not Mean Rejecting History, It Means Prioritizing A Direct Transmission Of Practice Over A Written Commentary About Practice. The Living Community Holds The Memory In Its Actions, Not In Books Written Centuries Later By Strangers. Therefore The Safer And More Honest Authority Is The Unbroken Tradition Passed By Generation, Not The Disputed Reports Compiled Long After The Fact.

response:
THE LONGEST BREATH

FADE IN:

INT. GOLDEN HALL OF RECORDS - DAY

A Massive Hall Lined With Flags Of Nations Long Forgotten. A Single Spot Light Cuts Through Hazy Air And Finds A Man In A Simple Wool Cardigan Sitting In A Wooden Chair. He Is 127 Years Old.

ELIAS MORA, 127, Skin Like Thin Paper Stretched Over A Map Of Veins, Holds A Trembling Hand To His Chest. A Crowd Of Journalists Hovers Like Moths.

ANNOUNCER (V.O.)
Ladies And Gentlemen, The Oldest Human To Ever Live.

Applause Erupts And Collapses Into Awe.

ELIAS
(Whispers)
I Thought I Would Feel More.

He Is Presented With A Glass Plaque. The Gold Foil Reads WORLD RECORD. He Smiles, A Thin Crack In His Lips.

CUT TO:

INT. NARROW APARTMENT - NIGHT

Rain Taps The Fire Escape. The Same Plaque Sits On A Kitchen Table Next To A Half Eaten Bowl Of Oatmeal. Elias Lies In Bed Under A Patchwork Quilt. The Ceiling Fan Clicks.

He Stares At The Dark.

FLASHBACK - MONTAGE

YOUNG ELIAS, 19, In A Cramped University Dorm, Dial-Up Modem Screeching. A Geocities Page Glows On His CRT Monitor. The Title Reads QUANTUM IMMORTALITY. He Reads With Wide Eyes.

BACK TO PRESENT

ELIAS (V.O.)
They Said If You Die, You Branch. The Universe Keeps The You That Survives. You Never Really Die, You Just Get Filtered.

He Pulls The Quilt Up To His Chin. His Chest Rises Slowly, Painfully.

ELIAS
(Softly)
So Why Am I Still Here?

He Tries To Sit Up. His Knees Buckle. He Clutches The Bed Rail.

ELIAS
If I Am Immortal, Then Why Does Every Breath Hurt? If I Am Immortal, Then Every Person I Loved Is Already Dead In A Branch Where I Am Not.

His Breathing Sharpens Into A Hiccup Of Panic.

ELIAS
Maybe I Am The Branch That Was Supposed To Die. Maybe I Am The Glitch. Maybe I Have Been Haunting Myself For 127 Years.

He Laughs, A Dry Rasp That Turns Into A Sob.

ELIAS
I Read It On The Internet In My Youth. I Thought It Was A Joke. Now The Joke Is Me. I Am Still Here. I Am Still Here. I Am Still Here.

He Pounds His Fist Against His Chest, As If Trying To Shake The Heart Loose.

ELIAS
Let Me Go! Let Me Go! Let Me Go!

The Plaque On The Table Shivers As If From A Tremor. Rain Hammers The Window.

He Closes His Eyes. The Room Is Silent Except For His Own Breathing, Counting Every Second He Should Not Have.

FADE TO BLACK.

THE END
